Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
243 AM EDT Sun Oct 25 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
A small but persistent area of stratocumulus is lingering near
and just west of I-95 in northern Virginia, and may expand a bit
through daybreak. Otherwise, the forecast is on track.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Below normal low temperatures give way to a warming trend
  early this week.

- 2) Above normal temperatures and dry conditions continue
  through the end of the week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Below normal low temperatures give way to a 
warming trend early this week. 

High pressure will drift southwest through Monday. As a result,
expect a continuation of frost and freeze conditions during the
overnight periods with seasonable temperatures during the 
daylight hours.

After a chilly start, temperatures will rebound well into the
60s for much of the area this afternoon. Some stratocumulus are
possible at times, but may ultimately be thin and transient.

High pressure will gradually drift southwest toward the central 
Appalachians tonight into Monday morning. Low-level flow will 
turn westerly allowing for less of a marine influence. This 
should set us up for one more good radiational cooling night 
before temperatures warm under return flow early in the 
workweek. Tonight will be more of a ridge-valley split type of 
night with cooler conditions in the valleys/cold pockets/locations
along and east of I-95 compared to the ridge tops given the 
sharp surface inversion/decoupling.

Only minor changes have been made to the previous min temperature 
forecasts, which are near or below the coldest guidance which 
performs best in radiational cooling (MOS, NBM 10th percentile and 
Canadian Regional).

Expect temperatures to rise above normal (upper 60s to lower 70s) by 
Monday afternoon as the warming airmass mixes to the surface. 
Minimal cloud cover and light winds will remain persistent.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Above normal temperatures and dry conditions 
continue through the end of the week.

An upper-level ridge will build through the middle of the week 
supporting above normal temperatures. A dry cold front will 
cross the area Tuesday, only dropping temperatures slightly. 
High pressure settles south of the area during the second half 
of the week supporting a warming trend again. A weak upper-level
disturbance will traverse the region Thursday night only 
bringing high clouds ahead of it. It looks like no precipitation 
will occur through the remainder of October.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Some ground fog could develop early this morning near IAD, MRB,
and CHO. Otherwise, expect VFR with some stratocu possible. NAM
and related guidance continues to show more widespread low CIGS
and fog late tonight into early Monday morning, with at least
some hint of this in other guidance and forecast soundings.

Winds will be light out of the NE this morning shifting to SE
this afternoon, then W overnight. W/NW winds AOB 10 kts Monday.

P6SM SKC with light and variable winds as high pressure dominates. A 
dry cold front will cross the area late Monday night with winds 
shifting to NW Tuesday.

&&

.MARINE...
Light northeast winds this morning will become southeast this
afternoon, then west overnight into Monday. No rain is expected
with light winds generally 10 knots or less.

Marginal SCA conditions possible Tuesday-Tuesday evening in NW
flow.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Light onshore flow will persist through this evening, and could
result in one last round of at or near minor flooding along
vulnerable shoreline this afternoon and evening.

&&
